judge_response:
ANALYSIS: “Hirschsprung’s disease” (with apostrophe-s) and “Hirschsprung disease” (without apostrophe-s) are both widely accepted variants in medical literature and clinical usage. Major authoritative sources — including the WHO International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10/ICD-11), UpToDate, Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, and the American Academy of Pediatrics — use “Hirschsprung disease” (non-possessive) as the preferred term, reflecting modern convention to avoid eponymous possessives. The apostrophe-s form is historically used but increasingly discouraged; however, it is not considered incorrect or ambiguous.

The core diagnostic entity — aganglionosis of the distal colon leading to functional obstruction — is identically denoted by both forms. There is no difference in clinical meaning, coding, or management implications.

VERDICT: CORRECT
